comparison: Both strongly support the DOz mouse population characterization and metabolic diversity (C1, C25-C29). OpenEval emphasizes breeding strategy and controls; peer reviewers praised the natural genetic diversity approach. OpenEval also covers methodological claims (C108-C112) that peer review addresses separately in R13.

Both support the proteomic characterization methodology (C31-C39). OpenEval highlights GAPDH variability as important control; peer reviewers requested methodological clarifications (trypsinization, normalization, CV comparisons) that were addressed. Both recognize the dataset as a key strength.

Both support linear modeling results and insulin sensitivity associations (C40-C48). OpenEval emphasizes statistical methodology and positive controls; peer reviewers found evidence 'compelling' but requested clarification on limited mitochondrial proteins in final fingerprint. OpenEval R3 covers C40-C48 while peer R3 extends to GSEA findings (C49-C53).

OpenEval R4 addresses GSEA results (C49-C53) with biological interpretation; peer R3 covers broader proteomic findings including these claims. Both support the findings, with peer reviewers describing systematic data utilization as strength.

Both support genetic mapping and pQTL filtering strategy (C54-C58). OpenEval emphasizes tissue specificity and translational relevance; peer reviewers requested justification for filtering criteria which was provided and accepted. Peer R4 also includes CMAP initiation (C59) not in OpenEval R5.

Both strongly support CMAP analysis and validation through known compounds (C59-C65). OpenEval highlights methodological rigor of filtered vs non-filtered comparison; peer reviewers praised integration with drug discovery and requested protein list details that were addressed.

Both support Prestwick screen methodology and thiostrepton identification (C66-C71). OpenEval emphasizes scoring matrix and dual assay validation; peer reviewers specifically praised the independent validation platform. OpenEval R7 includes validation data (C71) that peer review addresses in R7.

Both support ex vivo validation with diet-induced insulin resistance model (C72-C76). OpenEval emphasizes differential effects across muscle types/strains as specificity evidence; peer reviewers accepted the model characterization without concerns. OpenEval R8 extends to mechanistic findings (C77-C79) covered in peer R7.

Partial overlap on thiostrepton effects across muscle types (C77-C79). OpenEval supports differential effects as evidence of specificity; peer R7 covers broader thiostrepton findings (C5-C7, C71) and accepts variable effects as data. Both recognize preclinical support for new mechanism.

Both support insulin signaling analysis showing no effect on canonical pathways (C80-C82). OpenEval emphasizes consistency with palmitate-induced resistance model; peer reviewers requested discussion of direct vs indirect action and accepted mechanistic data as initial findings.

Both support metabolic flux analysis with Seahorse (C83-C88). OpenEval emphasizes differential effects on respiration vs glycolysis and logical interpretation; peer R8 covers broader mechanistic investigation including these metabolic findings.

Both support AMPK signaling analysis showing no effect (C89-C90). OpenEval notes appropriate positive control and cautious interpretation; peer R8 encompasses all mechanistic studies including AMPK, accepting them as initial findings requiring future detailed characterization.

Both support main proteomic findings from abstract (C2-C4). OpenEval links to detailed results and pathway analysis; peer R3 covers the underlying detailed findings with 'compelling' evidence assessment.

Both support main thiostrepton findings from abstract (C5-C8). OpenEval emphasizes validation experiments and qualified speculation; peer R7 highlights preclinical data for new mechanism and accepts initial mechanistic investigation.

Perfect agreement on validation through known insulin sensitizers (C91-C94). Both recognize these as positive controls strengthening confidence in the CMAP approach. OpenEval emphasizes their role as validation; peer reviewers note strong support for conclusions.

Both rate pathway interpretation (C95-C99) as supported but note mechanistic speculation requires validation. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN due to hypothetical mechanisms; peer reviewers accept interpretations as reasonable discussion points not challenged, though noting biological relevance accepted.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic hypotheses (C100-C102) being UNCERTAIN/speculative. Both recognize these as reasonable hypotheses requiring further investigation. OpenEval notes lack of direct evidence; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge future studies needed for detailed mechanism characterization.

Both support ARHGDIA/RAC1 findings (C103-C105). OpenEval emphasizes consistency with other protein findings and appropriate citations; peer R11 accepts these interpretations in discussion without challenge.

OpenEval supports background/introduction claims (C9-C24) with appropriate citations establishing scientific context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as these are standard literature citations not typically evaluated separately.

OpenEval supports Matsuda Index methodological choice (C106-C107). Peer R1 notes no concerns were raised about metabolic phenotyping or Matsuda Index use, implicitly supporting this methodological decision.

Both support data availability and methodological transparency (C114). OpenEval emphasizes reproducibility through repository access; peer R13 addresses broader methodological details including data sharing.

Peer R13 addresses methodological details (C108-C113) including normalization, randomization, and sample sizes that OpenEval distributes across R1 and R2. Reviewers requested clarifications that were provided and accepted.
